No.

If you want to be a part of the bleeding edge and love the gimmick factor of it, sure go ahead an spend the money.

But if you want to actually use it for 4K, don't bother. Save your money and get a high quality HDTV and be happy.

There is a lot of issues at play, primarily there is absolutely zero infrastructure for 4K home video. Broadcasters aren't even putting out uncompressed HD these days, much less 4K. 4K eats up 4x the bandwidth as HD unless you compress it and compression is the DEVIL! So assuming someone is broadcasting in 4K, unless they specifically say "uncompressed" or "lossless" then its probably going to look about the same as uncompressed HD or worse even.

When HDTV first rolled out there were a few stations that actually sent out true uncompressed HD, (HDNET FTW) and it was glorious. Now that most of the dial is pushing for HD, all that bandwidth (which was already pretty full) is even more clogged and next to no one wants to update their infrastructure. So HD is compressed and looks shitty compared to what it should. A large part of that wow factor is lost. 4K will have the same fate.

Secondly, with HD you could at least get movies in HD near the dawn of HDTV. I might be out of the loop, but I haven't seen a single 4K formatted player yet or discs to play in them. And don't tell me "the internet" because that bandwidth problem is back with a vengeance if you want to try and stream it off the web. EVERYTHING online is going to be lossy compressed and then stepped down to keep the stream alive. Assuming you do get true 4k pixels, the file itself is likely going to be compressed to something like H.264 (which is lossy).

And I'm not even getting into the whole "could be higher rez than your eye can see" issue. TL;RD: your eyes have a maximum acuity which is angular, so the farther you sit from a TV, the less resolution it needs, IE. 4K on a 50" TV you sit 15 feet from is totally useless.

I could be TOTALLY wrong here. I have been in the past. But IMO unless you WANT to blow money on bleeding edge gadgetry with no support, don't put money into 4K until there is infrastructure to support it properly.

We should get HD right and uncompressed before we move to 4K. If we can't even display HD without compressing it, we have no fucking business trying to display 4K.
